Explain the effect of increasing the pressure on the equilibrium yield of hydrogen iodide.

rows.answer:
Explanation linking (one mark each)
M1 yield no change
M2 same number of gas molecules on each side so position unchanged

parts.text:
The equation for a reaction is CO(g) + 2H₂(g) ⇌ CH₃OH(g)  ΔH = −91 kJ/mol

Explain the effect of increasing the temperature on the equilibrium yield of methanol.

rows.answer:
Explanation linking (one mark each)
M1 yield decreases
M2 forward reaction is exothermic so equilibrium shifts in the endothermic (backward) direction

parts.text:

M1 yield increases
M2 equilibrium shifts towards the side with fewer gas molecules (1 mol)

parts.text: Explain why a catalyst does not change the yield of a reversible reaction.

rows.answer:
Explanation linking (one mark each)
M1 it speeds up the forward and backward reactions equally
M2 so equilibrium is reached faster but position unchanged

parts.text: Explain why heating hydrated copper(II) sulfate and adding water to the anhydrous solid shows that the reaction is reversible.

rows.answer:
Explanation linking (one mark each)
M1 heating turns blue crystals white (water removed)
M2 adding water turns white powder blue again (and gets hot)

parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term dynamic in dynamic equilibrium.

rows.answer:
Explanation linking (one mark each)
M1 reactions are still happening / particles still reacting
M2 forward and backward rates are equal so no overall change
